faq_heading: Clayton condos and townhomes: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Clayton. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Clayton, Cloverdale: 96 condos and townhomes listed at the end of September 2026 and 20 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 21%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. By listings that is number 2 of 3 Cloverdale communities for condos and townhomes.

On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Cloverdale total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Listings of condos and townhomes in Clayton fell from 108 in June to 96 in September (−11.1%), and 96 sold across the 4 months. In September the community held 49.5% of Cloverdale’s 194 condos and townhomes listed.

blocks.text: Clayton home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

169 townhomes sold in Clayton with a median price of $760,000 (the middle half sold between $699,900 and $823,000), taking a median of 20 days to sell at 97.6% of the last list price; 7% sold above list. They had a median $489 per square foot, a median year built of 2012 and a median strata fee of $372 a month. 72 condos sold in Clayton with a median price of $464,400 (the middle half sold between $413,750 and $550,500), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 97.2% of the last list price; 1% sold above list. They had a median $616 per square foot, a median year built of 2013 and a median strata fee of $412 a month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Clayton

CLASSIFICATION NOTE (flagged up front): one in-area complex, Compass, is built in two forms under one name — apartment-condo buildings and townhouse units. Waterstone is also phased (2010 and 2015 parts), and Calera carries two different published unit counts (153 vs 95); both conflicts are stated in the entries, not smoothed over.
Waterstone — 6420 and 6440 194 Street, with the Waterstone-Esplanade phase at 6480 194 Street

Apartment/Condo, freehold strata, wood frame. The complex was built in phases: listings record the 6420/6440 buildings as built 2010 and the Esplanade building as built 2015, so any single "year built" for Waterstone is wrong. A building directory header describes a 274-unit development at the 6440 address; a complex-wide total covering all phases is UNCONFIRMED. Directory-listed amenities include a roughly 15,000 sq ft clubhouse with an indoor 60-foot pool, whirlpool, steam and sauna rooms, fitness facilities and a guest suite.
Calera — 18818 68 Avenue (complex name in listings: Calera / Calera Clayton at Village)

Apartment/Condo, freehold strata, built 2010. Published unit counts conflict: the building directory records 153 units, while an MLS data sheet for a unit in the same complex records "Units in Dev: Total 95" under strata plan BCS3888 — the exact per-strata unit count is UNCONFIRMED; quote neither figure as settled. Directory-listed amenities include a bike room, club house, exercise centre, in-suite laundry, recreation centre and storage.
Compass (apartment phase) — 18755 68 Avenue and 6815 188 Street

Listings classify 18755 68 Avenue as Apartment/Condo and 18777 68A Avenue as Row/Townhouse. A project source describes two four-level wood-frame buildings built in 2008 with 57 suites in the condo buildings and 104 homes in the whole complex including the townhouses; because that source blends the two forms, the apartment phase's own unit count is treated as UNCONFIRMED.
Yale Bloc — three buildings: 6468 195A Street (Yale Bloc 1), 6438 195A Street (Yale Bloc 2) and 19567 64 Avenue (Yale Bloc 3)

All three are Apartment/Condo, freehold strata, in the Clayton subdivision. Listings record Yale Bloc 1 as built 2016, Yale Bloc 2 as built 2018 and Yale Bloc 3 as built 2019; the project's original 2015 launch material describes three distinct buildings linked by an open courtyard with ground-level shops. Directory-listed amenities include a bike room, clubhouse and exercise centre. The directory's published restrictions read "pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed." A complex-wide unit count is UNCONFIRMED — no figure from a non-directory source was found.
Harlo — 19577 65B Avenue, with Building Two at 6585 195A Street per the developer's homeowner manual

By Steelix Developments, in East Clayton. Listing and manual material lists a rooftop terrace, fitness centre with a virtual studio, a golf simulator, a children's play area, community garden plots and underground parking. A directory header's "22-unit development" figure is inconsistent with unit numbers running into the 500s in the same building, so the total unit count is UNCONFIRMED and that figure is not used.

By Steelix Developments: 210 condominiums in five residential levels above about 15,931 sq ft of commercial space, studios to three bedrooms, 402–1,214 sq ft. The presale source states completion is "yet to be announced," so the completion date is UNCONFIRMED and no unit here is resale stock yet.

items.t: Clayton is a Surrey board sub-area in the Cloverdale community; the City of Surrey plans the same ground as Clayton Heights, a roughly 809-hectare (2,000-acre) plan area running from Fraser Highway south to the Agricultural Land Reserve to the north and west, with the Township of Langley at the east edge. The board's street-level boundary line itself is UNVERIFIED — it sits behind a members-only map layer.

The City divides the area into East Clayton, West Clayton and North Clayton neighbourhood concept plan (NCP) areas; East Clayton's NCP was endorsed in 2003 over about 314 hectares, West Clayton's was approved in July 2015 over about 288 hectares with 12,000+ future residents planned, and the North Clayton NCP has not yet been initiated.
Both NCP designation sets have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update — Surrey's current OCP is Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026, not the predecessor OCP.
The apartment-condo stock clusters along 68 Avenue, 194 Street and 195A Street in the older East Clayton core; the newest building, Harlo, sits in East Clayton near 65B Avenue and 195A Street.

Transit today is bus service on Fraser Highway and the collector grid; the Surrey Langley SkyTrain — a 16 km Expo Line extension from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City, anticipated in service in 2029 — will add two stations inside Clayton: Hillcrest-184 Street at the northwest corner of 184 Street and Fraser Highway, and the future Clayton Station at 190 Street and Fraser Highway.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Clayton

items.t: The Form B Information Certificate is the buyer's core document in every Clayton strata: under s. 59 of the Strata Property Act the strata must provide it within 7 days of a request, for a fee of no more than $35 plus up to 25 cents per page for copies. It is where the real numbers live — strata fees, contingency reserve fund (CRF) balance, parking and storage allocation, and any bylaw that actually applies to the unit.
Minimum CRF contribution: since November 1, 2023, stratas must contribute at least 10% of the annual operating fund to the CRF each year.

Rentals: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022. Where a directory line above says rentals are "allowed with restrictions" (Calera, Compass), the restriction half of that line no longer has legal effect; a strata can still regulate short-term rentals separately.

Age bylaws: the only age-restriction bylaw a BC strata may enforce is 55+, under ss. 123.1 and 123.2 of the Strata Property Act, with exemptions added May 1, 2023 (including for caregivers and for spouses/partners who met the rule when they moved).

Pets: pet limits remain lawful strata bylaws. Directory lines above state pets allowed with restrictions at Waterstone, Calera and Yale Bloc, a two-pet allowance at Compass, and dogs OK in a Harlo listing header — treat all of these as pointers only; the enforceable limit is the registered bylaw set attached to the Form B.

Zoning: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 governs. On July 8, 2024 the City renamed several residential zones (RF-12/RF-12C became R4; RF-SD became R6), so older Clayton documents may cite zone names that no longer exist in the current bylaw.

Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH): Surrey permits 3 units on lots under 280 m² and 4 units on lots over 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. This matters around Clayton's house lots, not inside the strata complexes. One secondary suite per house is permitted under the BC Building Code framework; in Surrey a suite is capped at 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area and is never permitted inside a coach or garden suite, and an unpermitted suite is not made legal by the SSMUH rules. Coach/garden suites run 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR), need lane access on smaller lots, and require one added parking space.
Short-term rentals in Surrey: owner-only, primary residence only, stays under 90 consecutive days, with a City business licence at $358 per year.

ALR edge: Clayton's north and west edges meet the Agricultural Land Reserve. On ALR land a principal residence is capped at 500 m² with one additional residence of 90 m² (lots of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (lots over 40 ha) — relevant to acreage buyers at the fringe, not to the strata stock.
Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty applied after July 2 and a further 5% after September 2.

GST on new builds is 5%. It applies to developer sales — including Harlo's developer units and Steelix on 188th presales — and not to ordinary resales. The first-time home buyers' GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026, per CRA Excise and GST/HST News No. 122) rebates 100% of the GST on a new home priced up to $1M (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5M, for agreements entered into from March 20, 2025 to 2031. The older GST New Housing Rebate covers homes the FTHB rebate does not: 36% of the GST, maximum $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000.

BC Property Transfer Tax: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% on the portion up to $2M, 3% above $2M, plus a further 2% on the residential portion of a price above $3M. The First-Time Home Buyers' exemption is full up to $835,000 fair market value (on the first $500,000) and partial up to $860,000; the Newly Built Home Exemption is full up to $1.1M and partial up to $1.15M — the exemption that matters for Harlo and Steelix on 188th purchases.

Federal first-time buyer tools: the Home Buyers' Plan allows a $60,000 RRSP withdrawal; the First Home Savings Account allows $40,000 lifetime at $8,000 per year. CMHC mortgage insurance premiums run 0.6%–4.5% depending on down payment and amortization.

Presales: REDMA gives a 7-day rescission period under s. 21 and requires purchase deposits to be held in trust under s. 18 — the framework that applies to Steelix on 188th contracts and to any developer-unit sale at Harlo.

blocks.text: Good to know about Clayton

items.t: The Clayton Community Centre at 7155 187A Street opened October 16, 2021 — 75,000 sq ft including a 14,000 sq ft library branch — and it is the amenity anchor the whole sub-area walks to; strata complexes here sell against it because most Clayton buildings have modest in-house amenities by comparison.

Waterstone is not one building of one age: the original 194 Street buildings date to 2010 and the Esplanade phase to 2015, so two units both marketed as "Waterstone" can be five years apart in envelope and warranty terms.

West Clayton is planned around a rapid transit station at 184 Street and Fraser Highway that does not exist yet — the plan was approved in July 2015 with 12,000+ future residents, and the SkyTrain now under construction is the delivery mechanism, anticipated in service in 2029. Land and presale pricing near 184 Street already trades on that station.

Older Clayton documents cite zone names that no longer exist: Surrey renamed RF-12/RF-12C to R4 and RF-SD to R6 on July 8, 2024, so a disclosure statement or older strata document quoting the old names is not necessarily wrong about the property — it is quoting a repealed label.

The area has three names for the same ground depending on who is speaking: Clayton (the board sub-area), Clayton Heights (the City's plan name) and East/West/North Clayton (the NCP names). A search run under only one name misses listings filed under the others.

Census figures for Clayton could not be verified in this research pass because the Statistics Canada profile host was unreadable at the time; any population or income figure for Clayton circulating without a working StatCan citation should be treated as UNCONFIRMED.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Clayton
Streets, schools and getting around Clayton

items.t: Clayton is a board sub-area of the Fraser Valley board community "Cloverdale" — the three sub-areas are Clayton, Cloverdale and Serpentine — and a neighbourhood inside the City of Surrey's Cloverdale community, one of the City's seven communities.

Municipal geography: the City plans this ground as Clayton Heights — the Clayton General Land Use Plan states Clayton Heights encompasses approximately 809 hectares (2,000 acres), extending from Fraser Highway in the south to the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) in the north and west, bordered by the Township of Langley in the east. The City's plan neighbourhoods are East Clayton, West Clayton and the not-yet-initiated North Clayton.

Clayton's ratios were the highest in the Cloverdale sub-area set that month (Cloverdale 13% / 17%; Serpentine NA in both). Cloverdale community medians (sub-area medians are not published: UNVERIFIED at sub-area level): detached $1,212,500; attached $740,000, $503/sq ft, 96% sale-to-list, 32 days on market.

Which of these schools fall inside the board's Clayton sub-area line (as opposed to the Cloverdale sub-area) is UNVERIFIED — no public board boundary exists to test addresses against. SD36 catchments are address-based and no locator run for a Clayton address is on record, so the catchment school for any specific address is UNVERIFIED.

Transit: no SkyTrain station is inside Clayton today. The Surrey Langley SkyTrain project names two stations serving Clayton directly — Hillcrest-184 Street Station, at the northwest corner of 184 Street and Fraser Highway, and Clayton Station, at the future intersection of 190 Street and Fraser Highway — and TransLink states the 16-kilometre Expo Line extension from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City has an anticipated in-service date of 2029.

ALR edge: Clayton Heights runs to the ALR in the north and west; the ALC housing frame for ALR parcels is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha), and ALR residences cannot be stratified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Clayton

items.t: : Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

Presales / new construction (REDMA): a presale buyer must receive the developer's disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18, deposits held in trust) and has a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging it (REDMA s. 21) — the frame for Steelix on 188th and any other developer sale surfacing in Clayton. Assignment consent and fees are contract terms: UNCONFIRMED until each disclosure statement is read.

blocks.text: Good to know about Clayton

items.t: "Clayton" has three names for the same ground. Clayton (board sub-area), Clayton Heights (the City's planning name) and East / West / North Clayton (the NCP names) — a search run under only one name misses listings and City documents filed under the others.

Clayton was the Cloverdale community's fastest shelf in September 2026. Clayton's sales ratios (29% detached, 21% attached) led the Cloverdale set that month, ahead of the Cloverdale sub-area (13% / 17%) — on medians published only at community level.

The municipal line runs through the neighbourhood's east edge. Two near-identical Clayton Heights streets can sit in different municipalities (Surrey vs Township of Langley) with different bylaws, taxes and school districts (SD36 vs SD35) — confirm which side of the boundary a listing sits on before comparing it to a cross-border comp.

The NCP labels are history, not current designations. The City records that the East Clayton (2003) and West Clayton (2015) NCP designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update — a listing quoting an NCP designation as current is quoting a superseded label; the OCP designation in COSMOS governs.
Any automated school list built from that field alone will misfile it.

Clayton Community Centre is the area's combined arts/recreation/library anchor. Clayton Community Centre, 7155 187A Street, officially opened October 16, 2021, is a 75,000 sq. ft. facility integrating arts, recreation and a full-service 14,000 sq. ft. Surrey Libraries branch — the amenity Clayton townhouse listings point to by neighbourhood name.

West Clayton was planned around a station that does not exist yet. The West Clayton NCP (approved July 2015, planned for over 12,000 residents) features a mixed-use urban centre adjacent to a future rapid transit station at 184 Street and Fraser Highway — the Surrey-Langley SkyTrain, anticipated in service in 2029, is the delivery mechanism, and land near 184 Street already trades on that plan.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Clayton?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 96 condos and townhomes listed in Clayton. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Clayton a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Clayton had a sales ratio of 21%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Clayton from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 96 condos and townhomes sold in Clayton over those 4 months, out of 165 in all of Cloverdale.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did townhomes in Clayton sell for?
faq.a: 169 townhomes sold in Clayton between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $760,000.

faq.q: How long do townhomes take to sell in Clayton?
faq.a: The median was 20 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.6% of the last list price (7% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Compass — is it condos or townhouses?
faq.a: Both, under one name. The 18755 68 Avenue phase is apartment condos; the 18777 68A Avenue units are Row / Townhouse in current listings.

faq.q: Can I rent out my Clayton townhouse?
faq.a: Long-term, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, whatever an older directory prints.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ townhouse in Clayton?
faq.a: No cross-referenced or queued complex is published as age-restricted — check the registered bylaws on the Form B before assuming either way.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Clayton townhouse?
faq.a: Run the exact address in the locator and never promise a school from the complex name.

faq.q: Are the old RF-12 zone labels in Clayton listings still current?
faq.a: No. Surrey's July 8, 2024 changes replaced RF-12 / RF-12C with R4 and RF-SD with R6. Check the lot's current zone in Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 before quoting small-lot or coach-house potential.
